sections.heading: ATP synthase, the maker
sections.body_md: The enzyme that actually produces ATP is called ATP synthase. It has two main parts: a rotor set in the membrane that spins as protons flow through it, and a head that sits in the mitochondrial interior and stitches ATP together. The spinning drives the chemistry.

sections.heading: The complexes that set it up
sections.body_md: ATP synthase cannot work alone. Four upstream complexes, numbered one through four, use energy from food-derived electrons to pump protons across the membrane. That built-up proton supply is what flows back through the rotor.

key_points: ATP synthase turns a proton flow into ATP.
Complexes I to IV build the proton supply it uses.
